_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

**Yes — this is already supported.** alphaTab can re-render only a bar window so bars outside that range are not drawn at all. That is separate from playback selection (which still shows the full score and highlights a range).

I created a worktree at `/Users/leocaseiro/Sites/alphaTabWebsite-partial-render-eval` on branch `eval/partial-bar-render`, with a small demo at `eval/partial-bar-render.html`.

## How it works

Use two display settings:

| Setting | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `display.startBar` | First bar to render (**1-based**, as shown on the sheet) |
| `display.barCount` | How many bars to render (`-1` = all remaining) |

For your example (10 bars total, show only bars 5–7):

```js
api.settings.display.startBar = 5;
api.settings.display.barCount = 3;
api.render();
```

Multi-track works the same way — combine with `core.tracks` or `api.renderTracks([...])`.

This is documented and demonstrated on the site:

- [Layouts showcase — “Page Layout (bar 5 to 8)”](https://alphatab.net/docs/showcase/layouts#page-layout-bar-5-to-8)
- [`display.startBar`](https://alphatab.net/docs/reference/settings/display/startbar) / [`display.barCount`](https://alphatab.net/docs/reference/settings/display/barcount)

The alphaTab source applies this in layout via `ModelUtils.computeFirstDisplayedBarIndex` / `computeLastDisplayedBarIndex`, and all page/horizontal layouts respect `firstBarIndex` → `lastBarIndex`. There are visual regression tests for bars 5–8 in `Layout.test.ts`.

## Display vs playback

These settings affect **visual layout only**. MIDI is still generated for the **full score**. If you also want playback limited to bars 5–7 (not just a selection overlay on the full score), set `playbackRange` separately using tick positions from `api.tickCache`:

```js
const score = api.score;
const lookup = api.tickCache;

const range = new alphaTab.synth.PlaybackRange();
range.startTick = lookup.getMasterBarStart(score.masterBars[4]); // bar 5
range.endTick = lookup.getMasterBar(score.masterBars[6]).end;   // bar 7
api.playbackRange = range;
```

## Caveats worth knowing

1. **Mid-score start** — The first visible bar gets system-start treatment (clef, key/time sig as needed). Bar numbers still reflect the original score (bar 5 stays “5”, not “1”).
2. **Full score stays in memory** — You are filtering at render time, not slicing the Guitar Pro model. That is usually what you want (fast re-render, no data loss).
3. **Repeats / jumps** — Starting mid-repeat can behave differently from a fresh import of just those bars; worth testing on your files.
4. **`barCountPerPartial`** — Unrelated; it controls lazy-render chunk size, not which bars are visible.

## Bottom line

| Goal | Supported? | Approach |
|------|------------|----------|
| Re-render so only bars 5–7 are visible | **Yes** | `startBar` + `barCount` + `render()` |
| Multi-track, same bar window | **Yes** | Same settings + track selection |
| Change range at runtime | **Yes** | Update settings, call `api.render()` |
| Playback only that range | **Partially separate** | Also set `playbackRange` via tick cache |
| Physically remove bars from the model | Possible but unnecessary | Model mutation; built-in settings are cleaner |

---

**Questions for you:**

1. Do you need **playback** scoped to the same bars, or is **visual-only** re-render enough?
2. Will users pick bar ranges dynamically (e.g. a “practice this section” UI), or is it fixed per view?
3. Any edge cases you care about — repeats, pickup bars, tempo/key changes at the slice boundary?

If you share a sample `.gp` file and the exact bar range, I can wire up a minimal proof in the worktree with your real data.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Done. There’s a bar-range demo on the site using **`display.startBar` / `display.barCount`** — no alphaTex conversion.

## What was added

**New showcase page:** `/docs/showcase/partial-bars`  
(run `npm start`, then open http://localhost:3000/docs/showcase/partial-bars)

**Component:** `src/components/BarRangeDemo/index.tsx`

It loads `canon-full.gp` (tracks 0 & 1), defaults to **bars 40–51**, and gives you:

- **From bar / To bar** inputs  
- **Re-render range** — updates the visible notation only  
- **Show all** — resets to the full score  
- **Play/Pause**  
- **Limit playback to selected bars** — optional; uses `playbackRange` via the tick cache  

## Approach (not alphaTex)

| | Display settings | alphaTex slice |
|---|---|---|
| **What it does** | Filters at render time; full GP stays in memory | Export/import a text subset |
| **GP features** | All preserved | Can lose layout, backing track, RSE, some effects |
| **Re-render speed** | Fast (`api.render()`) | Re-import each time |
| **Best for** | “Show bars X–Y of this file” | Authoring/editing notation as text |

For your use case, stick with display settings.

## Usage in your own code

```js
api.settings.display.startBar = 40;
api.settings.display.barCount = 12; // bars 40–51 inclusive
api.render();
```

Bar numbers are **1-based** (as printed on the sheet).

If you want this wired into the main playground (file picker + track selector) instead of a standalone showcase page, say the word.
